Subject: Delegation rollback trigger & DPA onboarding plan

Hi Samantha / CloudWorks procurement,

Thanks for sending over the revised MSA/order form redlines this morning. We've reviewed at a high level and want to confirm the flow-down items the customer flagged so we can route approvals internally and prepare the DPA updates. Key asks from the customer:

- Explicit subprocessor notification for any subcontracting that changes the data handling (they want 30 days notice).
- A rollback trigger: if a subprocessor cannot meet SOC2 evidence within 30 days, CloudWorks must either remediate or revert workloads to Redwood-managed endpoints.
- Clarified required evidence artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption-at-rest attestation, and a minimal audit log sample).

Attached is our working draft (redlined_orderform_v2.pdf) and a simple FLOWDOWN_MATRIX.xlsx that maps where each clause needs to appear (order form, annex, DPA).

Action items I propose:
1) CloudWorks to confirm whether the rollback trigger is operationally feasible (are there contractual constraints with your own subvendors?).
2) Redwood legal (Laura) to confirm acceptable wording for the rollback clause and for what constitutes a ‘remediation plan’.
3) Product (Rishi) to confirm technical feasibility and estimated timeline for a failover plan if remediation fails.
4) Sales/procurement (Priyom) to align on notice windows and commercial remedies (credits/termination).

Can we aim to have responses by end-of-day Thursday (2028-04-13)? If that's tight for you, propose alternate dates. I'll set up a short 30-minute call once we have CloudWorks' operational answer on the rollback.

Thanks,

--
Markus Klein

Markus —

Appreciate the clear summary and the matrix. Quick answers from the procurement/ops side:

- Notification window: 30 days is reasonable for most of our subvendor changes, but for a handful of carriers/legal entities we only get 14 days by contract. We'll enumerate exceptions and call them out in the FLOWDOWN_MATRIX.
- Rollback trigger: operationally this is non-trivial. We can build an automated traffic shift to Redwood-managed endpoints, but it will take ~6–8 weeks to instrument and test in our staging environment. For smaller subvendors we can implement manual rollback procedures in ~2–3 weeks.
- Evidence: we can provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report (date-limited), an encryption-at-rest attest, and a sampled audit log extract. We will need guidance on minimum fields you require in the log sample.

Questions for Redwood:
- Does your legal team have a preferred fallback timeline if remediation fails (e.g., 30 days remediation + 14 days to rollback)?
- What level of redaction is acceptable for SOC2 evidence?

We're looped in on the matrix now. I can also join a call if useful — propose Thu 13 Apr 10:00 or Thu 13 Apr 15:00 PT.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Procurement Operations
CloudWorks Inc.

Team —

Thanks Samantha, helpful details. A few legal notes after a quick pass of the redlines:

1) Rollback trigger timing: we should avoid a hard automation-only requirement in the MSA. Suggested language: CloudWorks must use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate within 30 days; if remediation is not reasonably possible, CloudWorks will work with Redwood on a documented rollback plan to move impacted traffic to Redwood-managed infrastructure within an agreed-upon window (we can capture a standard fallback of 14 business days unless otherwise agreed). This gives us flexibility while creating a contractual obligation to act.

2) Notice windows: propose a two-tier notice model in FLOWDOWN_MATRIX — 30 days for substantive subcontractor changes, 14 days for routine carrier or network provider swaps. We'll mark exceptions as Samantha flagged.

3) Evidence artifacts: acceptable items are redacted SOC2 Type II (redactions limited to internal personnel identifiers), encryption-at-rest attestation referencing key management controls, and an audit log sample with timestamps, resource identifiers, and event type. If CloudWorks can deliver a schema for the log sample, we'll confirm acceptance quickly.

4) Commercial remedies: sales/procurement — we should propose a short credits schedule tied to rollback failure and also preserve a right to terminate for material breach if remediation and rollback are both infeasible. Priyom, can you weigh in on the credit bands?

I'll prepare suggested MSA language and a DPA annex redline and upload to the Drive folder by EOD. If CloudWorks can confirm the log schema by EOD Thu, I can finish the annex Friday morning.

Laura Bennett
